Runway pricing per second

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

Official Runway plans, read Nov 15, 2026 PT from Runway's pricing page, are Free, Standard, Pro, and Max for individuals, plus Team and Enterprise. Standard is $15.00/month or $12.00/month billed yearly, with 625 credits a month. Pro is $35.00/month or $28.00/month billed yearly, with 2,250 credits. Max is $95.00/month or $76.00/month billed yearly, with 9,500 credits. There is no plan named Unlimited for new buyers. The official API, from official API pricing document, charges $0.01 per credit, or $0.05/s for Gen-4 Turbo and $0.12/s for Gen-4.5. On Max billed yearly, Gen-4.5 is $0.096/s if you use the month's credits. The cheapest Gen-4.5 row we track is a Krea yearly estimate, below that official API rate.

Last checked 2026-11-16. Official plan, compare-table, API, and help-center figures were read Nov 15, 2026 PT. Catalog rows below use the date on each row. See the Runway Gen-4 model page and the credit calculator for a 10-second Runway Gen-4 clip.

How much does Runway cost per second?

On Nov 15, 2026 PT, the public pricing page listed Free, Standard, Pro, and Max for individuals, plus a Team plan and an Enterprise tab. There is no plan named Unlimited for new buyers on that page. Free is $0 with 125 one-time credits that do not expire. Standard is $15/month, or $12/month billed yearly, with 625 credits a month. Pro is $35/month, or $28/month billed yearly, with 2,250 credits a month. Max is $95/month, or $76/month billed yearly, with 9,500 credits a month and a one-month rollover for unused credits. Team, from a separate Team page, is $69 per seat per month, or $55 per seat per month billed yearly, with 6,900 credits per seat per month for groups of two to nine. Enterprise pricing is custom and is not listed as a public dollar amount. Sources: https://runway.com/pricing and https://runway.com/team-plan.

The public pricing page, opened Nov 15, 2026 PT without signing in, has Individual, Team & Enterprise, and API tabs, and a Monthly / Yearly toggle. Yearly is 20% off the monthly price, billed once a year, with the same monthly credit allotment. A free plan sits at $0.00 with a one-time 125-credit deposit. Runway's pricing page. What do credits buy per second, and what does that cost on each plan?

The pricing-page compare table, read Nov 15, 2026 PT, lists credits per clip for each video model, with resolution or audio only when the label states them. Gen-4.5 and Gen-4 Video are 60 credits per 5 seconds (12 credits/s). Gen-4 Video Turbo is 25 credits per 5 seconds (5 credits/s). Aleph 2.0 is 140 credits per 5 seconds (28 credits/s). Veo 3.1 with audio is 320 credits per 8 seconds (40 credits/s). Dollar costs on a plan equal those credits times the plan's effective dollars per credit, and they assume every credit in that month's allotment is used. On Max billed yearly that is $0.096/s for Gen-4.5 and $0.04/s for Gen-4 Video Turbo. Standard and Pro credits reset each cycle, so unused credits raise the real cost. The dollar columns assume a 10-second clip is billed at the same credits-per-second rate as the published clip (5 seconds for most models, 4 seconds for Seedance 2.0, 8 seconds for Veo). If a model does not actually allow a 10-second output, that 10-second total would not apply.

The official API document, checked Nov 15, 2026 PT, sells credits at $0.01 each. Gen-4 Turbo is 5 credits/s ($0.05/s, $0.50 per 10 seconds). Gen-4.5 is 12 credits/s ($0.12/s, $1.20 per 10 seconds). Aleph 2.0 is 28 credits/s ($0.28/s) with a 56-credit minimum per generation. Those Gen-4 figures match the Runway API rows in our catalog. What does Unlimited's relaxed mode actually mean?

Two different things share similar names. The Unlimited plan is a legacy plan that is no longer offered to new buyers. Official help, updated August 27, 2026 and re-read Nov 15, 2026 PT, says eligible legacy Unlimited plans stay unchanged through November 30, 2026, then monthly plans move to Max at $95/month. That legacy plan included 2,250 credits plus Explore Mode (also called Unlimited Mode in the legacy article) for generations that do not use credits, at a relaxed rate: start times can be slower in busy periods, and the number of generations at once is limited. Veo 3 and Veo 3.1 were not available in that mode and required credits. Separately, a help article titled Generating in Unlimited Mode says Unlimited Mode is a generation mode, not the same as the legacy plan, and that this mode is currently available on Pro and Max. It may take longer to start and run fewer jobs at once. Which models it covers on Pro or Max can change with promotions and plan type; the article says to look for the Unlimited option in the session. A dollar cost per second cannot be computed for generations in that mode, because they are not billed in credits.

When is a route elsewhere cheaper?

For Runway's own Gen-4.5, the cheapest catalog row is a Krea yearly credit-plan estimate, which undercuts the official API's $0.12/s. Gen-4 Turbo's cheapest catalog row is the official Runway API at $0.05/s; we do not track a cheaper Turbo route. For models Runway also resells, including Kling 3.0, Wan 3.0, Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1, Grok Imagine, Gemini Omni Flash, and MiniMax Hailuo, other APIs or credit plans in the catalog are often cheaper than Runway's API. How do we calculate this?

Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
